source.title: Placebo analgesia and its opioidergic regulation suggest that empathy for pain is grounded in self pain.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: Strongest causal (not merely co-activation) evidence that other-directed pain affect runs through the self-pain system: placebo analgesia lowered both first-hand pain and empathy for pain, with reduced anterior insula / midcingulate engagement, and naltrexone reversed both. This is the closest human analogue to 'other-bound suffering = own suffering stream + binding'. Held below 0.7 because effect sizes on empathy ratings were modest, it is one lab's paradigm, and it shows dependence on the self-pain channel, not that the other-model binding slot is the only additional ingredient.
failure_signatures: Placebo expectation could lower general negative affect or rating tendency rather than the specific shared pain channel; the naltrexone reversal constrains but does not exclude this.
Shows dependence of empathy on self-pain machinery, not sufficiency: it cannot show that other-bound affect is NOTHING BUT the self stream plus binding.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Experimentally reducing first-hand pain via placebo analgesia reduces empathy for another's pain and AI/MCC responses; blocking placebo analgesia with the opioid antagonist naltrexone normalises empathy, suggesting pain empathy is grounded in self-pain neural function and neurochemistry.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct support for MECH-405's core routing assertion: dampening the agent's own suffering stream (SD-011 analogue) should dampen other-bound suffering in the same proportion. Gives a concrete REE falsifier: an attenuation of the self harm/suffering channel that leaves other-bound affect intact would refute the routing claim.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human adults with explicit empathy ratings; REE's other-model binding slot (ARC-083) has no identified correlate here. Supports the shared-stream half of the claim only; the attribution/binding half is untested by this design.
mapping.source_context: fMRI RCT (n=102) plus psychopharmacological follow-up (n=50) with naltrexone; Vienna social neuroscience group.

confidence_components.notes: Causal manipulation in a large sample; maps closely to the routing half of the claim; transfer risk from human rating paradigm.
